paragraphs.text: Dear elders and sisters, just excited to share some more from this great book with you tonight. But before I get into that, I want to tell you I enjoyed with all the other mission presidents and Area Seventy in the Philippines a wonderful two and a half hour Zoom conference today this morning, where we went through mission by mission, how they're doing it, and what's happening in the missions, and what an inspiring experience to hear from the missions that don't have smartphones, how they're working hard, they're doing some very, very innovative things and it's just—it's great to see it and you should be really, really proud to be a part of a missionary generation that can do it with the smartphones and can actually get out there and be highly productive, even if they don't have that technology, and that's just—it was just wonderful to hear about.

Obviously, these are difficult times in terms of our ability to do the things that we used to do and to have the kinds of interactions that we used to have, but they're great opportunities for learning. And as we talked about this, we shared the Quezon City North experience, which I think has been pretty helpful around the Philippines, but I think the key thing is that all the mission presidents are receiving inspiration and revelation and are tapping into the collective inspiration and faith of the missionaries, and so we're seeing good things happen. It's just also wonderful to see how well our stake presidents and bishops are doing and just the wonderful members of the Church in the Philippines. So it's in many ways a hard time, but in other ways it's a fantastic time to see the character and the quality of the kind of people that we get to call our brothers and sisters.

Now let's jump into chapter two. This is a longer chapter. We won't go through the whole chapter, but we'll be covering the key part of the first elements of this chapter. It's entitled, Faith and the Power of Heaven. It goes like this and again, I'll break in and out of the text of the book with my own comments and thoughts from time to time, and I'm going to try to speak more slowly than I did yesterday.

Once you develop a basic faith in the overall plan of salvation, repent, acquire a testimony in the restored gospel, and live in harmony with the gospel, you are now in a position to exercise the necessary faith that unlocks the powers of heaven.

So stepping away from the book here, you see a process here. You develop faith in the overall plan of salvation. You repent, you get a testimony, and then you're obedient to the principles of the gospel. And when you've done these things, you're now able to exercise that faith that you are developing. And like all exercise, it builds whatever it is you're exercising. If you exercise a muscle, the muscle gets bigger. If you exercise focus, focus gets stronger. If you exercise your mental capacities, they get better, stronger, bigger. You get the point. And so you develop the basic faith and then you get your life in harmony and live in accordance with the gospel, and now you're in a position to exercise your faith, which will grow it.

Back to the text. With these powers, you'll be able to accomplish righteous desires that require the Lord's help, such as securing a good job, overcoming a bad habit, seeing someone that you love converted to the gospel, speaking by the power of the Holy Ghost in such a way that people are highly influenced when they hear what you're teaching. Unless you exercise sufficient faith, you actually deny the Lord the opportunity to help you in the course of your daily life.

The scriptures teach us that certain powers of heaven are governed by the faith of mortal men and women. For instance, Ether 12:18: "And neither at any time hath any wrought miracles until after their faith." In First Nephi 7:12: "...the Lord is able to do all things according to his will, for the children of men, if it so be that they exercise faith in him..." In Moroni 10 verse 7: "...deny not the power of God; for he worketh by power, according to the faith of the children of men." In Second Nephi chapter 27, verse 23: "For behold, I am God; and I am a God of miracles; and I work not among the children of men save it be according to their faith." In Moroni 7:33: "And Christ hath said: If ye will have faith in me ye shall have power to do whatsoever thing is expedient in me." And then finally, this one from the Doctrine and Covenants section 8, verse 10: "Remember that without faith you can do nothing."

So Moroni thoroughly understood the role of faith in releasing the powers of heaven. This is evident in his response to a revelation he received regarding his ability to overcome his weaknesses. We often quote that very special verse, Ether 12:27, when he gets that revelation, the Lord speaking to him about his weaknesses. But this is what Moroni says back to the Lord afterwards, and you can find this in Ether 12 verse 29 and 31:

"And I, Moroni, having heard these words, was comforted, and said: O Lord, thy righteous will be done, for I know that thou workest unto the children of men according to their faith; For thus didst thou manifest thyself unto thy disciples; for after they had faith, and did speak in thy name, thou didst show thyself unto them in great power."

Jesus also performed miracles according to the faith of the people as is shown throughout the scriptures in the New Testament and in Third Nephi. It is important that we all understand that the influence of the powers of heaven in our lives is governed, or I should say, probably controlled by faith. In other words, the Lord's hands are essentially tied until you exercise faith in him. Just as faith without works is dead, James 2:14 to 20, works without faith are dead since they are not sustained by the powers of heaven.

The Lord has said that if we have fears in our hearts, if we have doubts, we actually deny ourselves the blessings of heaven. You can find that in Doctrine and Covenants section 67, verse 3. For example, look at this as an example. If you lack faith, you can spend hours and hours preparing to teach a lesson to a family of investigators and still not be very effective in touching the hearts of the investigators. No matter how much time you devote to a task, your ultimate level of achievement is limited unless you learn to exercise the faith required to bring in the strength and power from God, which is available to each of us.

The author says, I would estimate of those members of the Church who are motivated to pay a full tithing, there are significant numbers who in turn deny themselves the full blessings that come from the payment of tithing because they failed to exercise faith sufficient to allow the Lord to bless them for obedience to the law of tithing.

This is important, elders and sisters. What the author is saying and what I would agree 100% with him on in this is that there are people who are faithful tithers. They pay an honest tithing, but they don't receive all the blessings available to them because they don't exercise faith in the promise of the Lord to bless them in obedience for their payment of tithing. I've seen it personally in the lives of people when I've been a bishop or a stake president and I've seen faithful tithers who didn't get the job that they should have got. They didn't get the raise in their employment. It was because their faith just was sufficient to motivate them to pay the tithing but not sufficient to draw down the powers of heaven to bring those blessings into their lives. We've got to go beyond that faith that is just a driver of action.

So back to the text. You must realize that the payment of tithing is compliance with only part of the law. The full law requires us to have faith that makes it possible for the Lord to bless us for paying our tithing. The same principle holds true when we administer to the sick. The Lord does not bless the person beyond the combined faith of those associated with the administration. Certainly there are many blessings the Lord would love to extend to each individual member of the Church if they would merely exercise the faith that would allow him to extend those blessings. In other words, our righteous living, the actual work we do, the actual obedience that we do generally exceeds—and this is so true in the Church—the work we do, the obedience we do, the effort that we make generally exceeds our faith. If our faith were greater, we would receive more blessings which the Lord wishes to have us have and which we have qualified for as a result of our righteous living. This is such an amazing principle that we have to get through our heads.

Back to the text. Let's consider a missionary faced with the task of learning a foreign language. Faith will give that missionary the assurance that he or she can learn the language if he or she applies himself to the task. So this is the faith to take action. If he relies on the faith that motivates him to action exclusively, in fact, if that's the only level of faith he operates with, the time that it takes him to be able to converse in the language will be determined solely by his own ability, and it could take a very long time. And you've seen that in the foreign missionaries that came in. Those of you who've been in the mission for a while, you saw foreign missionaries that came into the mission and some of them learned the language very quickly and some of them took a long time. I wonder why that might have been. I think we're seeing maybe a reason for it.

However, if the missionary exercises the faith to action and the faith necessary to call down the powers of heaven to assist in the learning of the language, that missionary's ability to learn the language is facilitated or actually increased by the power of heaven. In this case, the Spirit or the gift of tongues, and he will become conversant in the language in a much shorter time. The role of faith to motivate as well as the role of faith to power applies to all learning. Through the powers of heaven, our intellectual abilities can be magnified.

I've seen this in a number of people's lives. I've seen it in my life. If we have the faith to take the action to learn and we have the faith to draw upon the powers of heaven, the Spirit literally increases our ability to learn. Our intellectual capacities are increased. In addition, the Lord has said that we can be, quote, "taught from on high," close quote, if we seek specific knowledge by means of the prayer of faith. That's found in Doctrine and Covenants section 52 verse 9. Through the powers of heaven, insights and understandings can be revealed to our minds. This promise applies to all areas of inquiry, not just religion.

For example, I mean, when you're a parent and you're a new parent, you've never been a parent before. You don't know how to raise children. You're learning as you go. And there are books, but maybe not books specific to what you actually need to know for your specific child in that child's specific trial or challenge or circumstance that's difficult. Through the power of faith, you can not only learn from the world's learning, but you can draw upon heaven and learn through revelation exactly what you need to do to help that child. I've seen this in Sister Hughes and in my role as parents for our eight children numerous times. There was only one way to learn something we needed to learn on many occasions with our children, and that was through the powers of heaven. And it was drawn by faith to that power, not just faith to action.

So let's look at the role of faith in inspiration itself or revelation. If a person is faced with a difficult decision, faith can motivate that person to pray, in other words, faith to action, and seek guidance from his Father in Heaven. However, unless that person exercises the faith required to call down the powers of heaven, the Lord cannot inspire him regarding his problems.

Ever wonder sometimes when you may not get an answer to prayer? Maybe it's the Lord's timing that's involved, but maybe you're not exercising your faith. I remember an experience with two missionaries that went home some time ago. They're both Polynesian missionaries and Elder Hopoate and Elder Filawaki were working together. And a lot of the Polynesian missionaries had great faith. It's been one of the trademarks of that nationality for as long as I've been in the church and knowing about it. They seemed to have great faith, just faith to do miracles.

And they were telling me the story about how they had prayed to know where they should work that day. They were struggling to get some things going in their area. They prayed, should we go here? Should we go there? They had the thought they should go to an area they hadn't been to before. And they were in that area and walking along. And all of a sudden Elder Filawaki said to his companion, Elder Hopoate, "Elder, stop. Let's say a prayer right now." And so right there on the side of the road, they prayed where they should go. And then they started walking again and they walked a few, you know, maybe 20 or 30 feet. And then Elder Filawaki said, "I think we need to talk to the people in this house right here." And Elder Hopoate was like, "Really?" And Elder Filawaki was like, "Yeah, these are the people." And they went in there and sure enough, those people were at church the next Sunday, they went on to receive the gospel. And as far as I know, they are active members of the Church to this day.

Now, this is interesting because they had the faith to action, i.e. to pray to seek help. And then they had the faith to action again to pray right there in the area. But then they had to have the faith, in the case of Elder Filawaki, he had to have the faith to say, "This is the place." Now, I think that's interesting. In other words, an individual governs—your faith governs a very large amount of whether or not you receive inspiration to help you solve the problems in your life or to accelerate your success in life.

Another example could be given of just a regular member of the Church who's prompted to invite a non-member friend of his to join the Church. Faith can motivate the person to spend time with a non-member, to fellowship the non-member in all the outward respects. And through the power of faith, the Church member can now request that the non-member be touched by the Spirit, separate from any actions on the part of the member. The non-member receives his own spiritual inspiration, which then prompts him to investigate the gospel. We see examples of this in the scriptures, and I'm pretty sure that all of us can find examples of this in our missionary service.

In each of these examples, it's easy to see the role of faith in motivating a person to take action, and also the role of faith as a principle of power in drawing on the powers of heaven. In the future, you should make a special effort to analyze the role of faith in your endeavors. You should make a conscious effort to analyze the role of faith in motivating you to action, and instances when the situation requires faith as a principle of power.

So what we really want to get out of this section of the book is making a clear distinction between these two levels of faith: faith to action, faith that motivates us to get up in the morning and do our work, study, and do all the different things, pray, all the different things that require outward action on our part. But also, we need to very carefully understand and see, make that distinction, to that next level of faith where we go to the Lord in humility, but boldly seeking added strength and power from him in form of inspiration, in the form of intervention, in the form of just expanding our capacity, that allows us to go beyond our mortal ability, or reach beyond our mortal actions such that other people are influenced through the power of the Spirit. That's what we really want to make sure we get.

As we make this distinction in our lives, day to day, see where it works on the one level, see where we need to apply it on the other level, we become more aware of faith as a principle of power, not just as a principle of action. So you should consistently call upon the Lord to assist you in achieving righteous desires. As I often have said to you, think big, because with the Lord nothing is impossible to you. There is no righteous desire that he can't bring about into your life if you have the faith to action and the faith to draw upon the powers of heaven.

So as we conclude here, I want you to think about this question and discuss it with your companion and your kabahis. What governs the powers of heaven as they relate to the achievement of righteous desires? Elders and sisters, we love you. Grateful to be able to share these thoughts with you in this great little book with you. I hope you're finding inspiration from it and understanding from it. Have a great night. Enjoy yourself. Sleep well. Let's make tomorrow a great day.
